title: finding(scripts): `check-installed-spec-pin-claims`'s LEDGER has no class for a claim naming a version AHEAD of the pin — and the gap points the next reader at the one remedy the gate itself calls worse
body:
`scripts/check-installed-spec-pin-claims.mjs` has **no class for a claim that names a version AHEAD of the resolved pin**, and the gap steers the next reader toward the one remedy the gate's own docblock calls worse than the defect.

## Measured by the seat on the objectui#9874 branch (`2de140b9f`), ⛔ not relayed

- `LEDGER_CLASSES` is a **closed set of two** — `:438`, `export const LEDGER_CLASSES = ['stale', 'historical'];` — and `:941` fails any entry outside it.
- The roster now carries **51** entries (control: 51 `class:` lines in the same block, same command). Their versions: `17.0.0-rc.0` ×1 · `17.0.0-rc.1` ×1 · `17.0.0-rc.5` ×4 · `17.0.0-rc.6` ×6 · `17.0.0` ×11 · `17.1.0` ×4 · `17.2.0` ×21 · `17.3.0` ×2 — **all at or below the resolved pin `17.4.0`** (`pnpm-lock.yaml`) — and exactly **one at `17.5.0`**, the entry objectui#9874 added.

⇒ ⭐ every entry but one describes a version this repo has already passed. The word `historical` fits them; it reads as 「about the past」 and the new one is about a release this repo has ⛔ **not installed yet**.

## Why the gap is worth a card rather than a comment

The gate's own docblock, `:31`–`:34`, verbatim:

> **"when it changed"** — … These are permanently true. A gate that "fixes" them rewrites history into a falsehood, and that is strictly worse than the stale claim it replaces.

An agent that reads the closed set as a dead end — 「neither class fits a forward claim」 — reaches for the other remedy the gate offers: **re-measure and restamp**. On a *retirement* sentence that writes a fresh falsehood: restamping 「`@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 retired `view.list.navigation.view`」 to the resolved `17.4.0` asserts that 17.4.0 retired the key, when 17.4.0 is precisely the version where the key still **exists**. ⇒ the gap does ⛔ not merely cost a naming argument; it points at the failure mode the file exists to prevent.

## The two shapes a fix could take — ⛔ this card does not choose

- a **forward-looking class** beside `stale` / `historical`; or
- **one sentence in the module docblock** saying `historical` covers 「names a release, past or future」.

⚠️ Either is a change to a gate's declared vocabulary, so it is the claiming seat's measurement and ⛔ not this seat's preference.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

⛔ Not that the gate is wrong to have caught objectui#9874's sentence — it caught a real drift, the ledger entry is the sanctioned remedy, and the gate was ⛔ not weakened, skipped, quarantined or narrowed. ⛔ Not that `historical` is the wrong class for that entry: with the reasoning written into the entry's own `why`, it is defensible today. The defect is that the **next** reader has to re-derive that reasoning from scratch, against a closed set that reads as excluding them.

## Dedupe words

`installed-pin-claims ledger class ahead of pin` · `LEDGER_CLASSES historical forward` · `claim names unreleased version` · `check-installed-spec-pin-claims class set` · `restamp retirement sentence falsehood`
